Bug_Title: Only one method invocation is expected when testing checked exceptions
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the showBug method where both f(1) and g(f(1)) can throw an IOException, making it unclear which method is expected to throw the exception.
Trigger_Explanation: The generated JUNIT test case triggers the bug by calling the 'g' method with arguments that cause it to throw an IOException, while ensuring that only one method invocation is responsible for the exception.

Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test results show that only one test failed (testShowBugFThrowsException), indicating that the expected IOException was not thrown as anticipated. This does not confirm that the bug was triggered because the test was set up to check for an exception from g(-1), which indeed throws an IOException, but the test framework expected an exception and did not receive one, leading to a failure. There is no evidence in the test results that multiple method invocations caused ambiguity about which method threw the exception.
